name: RT-2 Vision-Language-Action (VLA) Models
observations: Source: 'RT-2: Vision-Language-Action Models Transfer Web Knowledge to Robotic Control' (Brohan et al., Google DeepMind, 2023, arXiv:2307.15818). Studied from local PDF in pdf/embodied_ai_papers.

Core idea: Co-fine-tune a large pretrained vision-language model (VLM) on BOTH internet-scale vision-language data (VQA/captioning) AND robot trajectory data so a single end-to-end model maps robot observations to low-level actions while retaining web knowledge.

Key recipe — 'actions as text tokens': robot actions are discretized and expressed as language tokens, letting the same model, tokenizer, and weights handle language and control with no action-only layers. This defines the VLA model class.

Action encoding: 8 dims = 6-DoF end-effector delta position (x,y,z) + rotation (x,y,z) + gripper extension + discrete 'terminate' command. Continuous dims discretized into 256 uniform bins; rendered as a space-separated string, e.g. '1 128 91 241 5 101 127'.

Token reservation: PaLI-X already has unique tokens for integers <=1000 (reuse them for action bins); PaLM-E overwrites its 256 least-frequently-used tokens with action tokens (a form of symbol tuning).

Co-fine-tuning (vs naive robot-only fine-tuning) is a critical trick: mixing web data with robot data preserves VLM concepts, prevents catastrophic forgetting, and yields more generalizable policies; robot data is up-weighted in each batch.

Output constraint: at inference, when prompted with a robot-action task the decoder is restricted to sampling only valid action tokens; full natural-language vocabulary remains available for standard VLM tasks.

Training I/O format: input = camera image + task text in VQA format 'Q: what action should the robot take to [instruction]? A:'; output = string of action tokens. Data: RT-1 robot demos (13 robots, 17 months, office kitchen) + web VQA/captioning data.
Instantiations: RT-2-PaLI-X (5B and 55B) and RT-2-PaLM-E (12B). Evaluated over ~6,000 real-world trials on a 7-DoF mobile manipulator.
Real-time inference: largest 55B model served on multi-TPU cloud, queried over network, running 1-3 Hz; the 5B variant runs ~5 Hz. Cloud inference enables serving multiple robots.

Results: strong generalization to unseen objects, backgrounds, and environments (~2x better than RT-1/MOO, ~6x better than representation baselines); emergent capabilities incl. symbol understanding ('move apple to 3'), reasoning (visual 'cup with same color', math 'sum of two plus one', multilingual), and human recognition ('person with glasses').

Chain-of-thought: augment data with a 'Plan:' step in natural language before action tokens (e.g., 'Instruction: I'm hungry. Plan: pick rxbar chocolate. Action: ...'), enabling multi-stage semantic reasoning (choose a rock as a hammer, an energy drink for a tired person).

Takeaway: VLM/web pretraining can be transferred directly into closed-loop low-level robot control by unifying action and language in one token space — the blueprint followed by modern open VLAs (OpenVLA, pi0, SmolVLA).

name: LeRobot (Hugging Face)
observations: Open-source library (Context7 ID /huggingface/lerobot) making end-to-end robot learning accessible; the closest current best-practice toolkit for RT-2-style VLA workflows.
Supports VLA and imitation-learning policies: SmolVLA, pi0, pi0.5, ACT, and Diffusion Policy.
End-to-end workflow: Teleoperate -> Record (synchronized camera + actions dataset) -> Train -> Deploy via CLIs lerobot-record, lerobot-train, lerobot-rollout (pip install lerobot).
VLA training example: lerobot-train --policy.path=lerobot/smolvla_base --dataset.repo_id=... --batch_size=64 --steps=20000 (SmolVLA fine-tune ~20k steps / ~4h on one A100).
Real-Time Chunking (RTC) inference backend (--inference.type=rtc) gives smooth continuous motion for high-latency VLAs like pi0/pi0.5/SmolVLA, analogous to RT-2's cloud-inference latency handling.

name: Hugging Face Transformers (VLM/VLA backbone)
observations: Provides the pretrained VLM backbones behind modern VLAs (e.g., PaliGemma, LLaVA, Idefics2) composed of a vision tower (CLIP/SigLIP) + multimodal projector + LLM decoder — architecturally the same family RT-2 co-fine-tuned (PaLI-X/PaLM-E).
Hosts OpenVLA-style vision-language-action models and shared AutoModel/pipeline APIs for multimodal image-text processing usable as a base for RT-2-style action-as-token fine-tuning.
